paragraphs: Cognyte sells investigative analytics software to government agencies and other organizations. The company says hundreds of customers in approximately 100 countries use its software to run investigations into threats to national security and into criminal and terror activity. Its press releases describe those customers as law enforcement, national security and military intelligence agencies.

At the center of the portfolio is an investigative analytics platform that fuses large-scale, varied data into one picture of people, places, organizations and events. It tracks, tags and alerts analysts to changes in that picture using artificial intelligence and machine learning. Information and case management policies are meant to keep work compartmentalized while teams collaborate. One solution line, network intelligence, draws insights from fragmented data captured from a range of communication networks. Another, operational intelligence, gives field units real-time insights while a mission is under way. A separate product, LUMINAR, supplies external threat intelligence to national security operations centers and to sectors such as critical infrastructure, telecom and financial services.

Cognyte Software Ltd. trades on Nasdaq under the ticker CGNT, and its press releases are issued from Herzliya, Israel. The homepage cites 30 years in the market behind the platform and the solutions built on it. Among recent news items, the company says one of the largest state law enforcement agencies in the United States selected it under a contract announced in March 2026.

quote.text: Hundreds of customers in approximately 100 countries rely on Cognyte’s solutions to accelerate and conduct investigations and derive insights, with which they identify, neutralize and tackle threats to national security and address different forms of criminal and terror activities.
